summary: Douglas County, OR lookout on Dean Mountain in the Elliott State Forest; cupola cabin 1920s, 1946 tower, removed or destroyed 1966.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden tower with 8-by-8 cab and cabin (1946 replacement of a cupola cabin)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1966; no source we read describes the site today

events.note: Original shake cabin, built around 1914 per the Elliott page
Forest Service used the summit from about 1915 (Elliott page); June and August 1915 newspaper items describe a planned outlook station and a telephone line to the lookout station
Elliott page dates a ground-based 16-by-16 cupola cabin to 1920
Register and firelookout.com date a 20-foot cupola cabin to 1922
Coos Forest Protective Association takes over fire protection from the Forest Service
Cupola cabin replaced by a 20-foot wooden tower with an 8-by-8 cab and a cabin
Six teenage boys apprehended after a severe case of vandalism at the lookout; case cleared up (September 1966 item)
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Elliott page gives no method for Dean's Mountain
Registered December 9, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the 20-foot cupola cabin to 1922; the Elliott page dates a 16-by-16 cupola cabin, which it calls a replacement for a shake cabin of about 1914, to 1920. The sources disagree and the story says so.

The register says the lookout was removed in 1966 and firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. The Elliott page says the state removed or burned Elliott lookouts, without naming Dean's Mountain, so the story reports the disagreement without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree: 1922 (register, firelookout.com) vs 1920 (Elliott page); the Elliott page also gives the cabin as 16 by 16 feet where the register says 20-foot cupola. Removal is 1966 in both register and firelookout.com, but removed vs destroyed differs and no source describes the site today. Record ownership is 'unknown'; the Elliott page indicates the Department of State Lands manages the Elliott State Forest, which the story does not state as ownership. Record agency Coos FPA matches the register. The Elliott page gives the summit as 1,818 ft; the story uses 1,819 ft from the register and firelookout.com. The Phillips book is cited only through the Elliott page; the CougarPass.Org PDF could not be read by fetch_text and was not used.
